chains.title: Candidate CREB3L4-mediated effect; regulatory element and target unresolved

links.claim: CREB3L4 is the leading named candidate here because it is expressed in MCF7 and has an own-model QBiC-SELEX result predicting stronger in-vitro binding to ref C than alt T; a separate model mapped from CREB3L2 also favors ref, but neither result establishes occupancy, and no variant-overlapping CREB3L4 peak is reported.
A regulatory element overlapping the variant is not established; this chain would require an unannotated element not detected in the supplied annotations.
No target gene can be assigned from the supplied evidence; PELI2 is nearby, but proximity does not establish regulation by this variant.
MCF7 is a candidate context because CREB3L4 is expressed there, although locus occupancy or activity in MCF7 is not shown.
A breast-cancer consequence is hypothetical; the supplied evidence does not connect this variant or a target gene to breast cancer.

predictions: If this chain is correct, an endogenous-locus assay in relevant breast cells should detect CREB3L4 occupancy, with more occupancy on ref C than alt T.
A regulatory effect should depend on CREB3L4 more than on TGIF1 or TET3; the target gene and the direction of any expression change are not specified by current evidence.
falsified_if: Sensitive assays in relevant cells find no CREB3L4 occupancy or no ref-favoring allelic occupancy at the locus.
CREB3L4 perturbation does not alter a reproducible variant-dependent regulatory effect.

matrix.test: Targeted TF-specific CUT&RUN-qPCR at the endogenous locus in MCF7 cells, measuring allelic occupancy for CREB3L4, TGIF1, and TET3 (using a suitable heterozygous line or reciprocal allele-edited cells).

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible variant-overlapping occupancy with a consistent allele imbalance for these candidate TFs.
CREB3L4 occupancy is detected and is higher on ref C than alt T.
TGIF1 occupancy is detected and is higher on ref C than alt T.
TET3 occupancy is detected and is higher on ref C than alt T.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent reporter effect, or no candidate-TF-specific dependence.
